faqs.a: Select the text you want to format, then click a toolbar button — for example B for bold or H1 for a heading. Formatting applies to the selection, or to the next text you type.
faqs.q: How do I format my text?

faqs.a: Yes. The download button saves a complete, standalone HTML file with your content that opens in any browser.
Click the Copy button to copy the formatted HTML source, then paste it into your website editor, blog or email template.
faqs.q: Can I use this text on my website?

faqs.a: Rich text is only plain characters plus formatting — there is no way to upload or embed images. Use the Strip HTML Tags tool to convert rich text back to plain text.
faqs.q: Can I add images to my document?

faqs.a: The editor uses your browser's native editing engine. Minor differences in list styling or spacing between Chrome, Firefox and Safari are normal.
faqs.q: Does it look the same in every browser?

faqs.a: No. The editor does not auto-save. Download your document as HTML if you want to keep it.

online-text-editor.formula:
words = count of whitespace-separated tokens in visible text
chars = total visible characters
html = serialized DOM of the editing area
howTo: Click inside the editor and type, or paste existing text.
Select text and use the toolbar: B/I/U for style, H1/H2 for headings, bullets, alignment, size and color.
Use the X (eraser) button to remove formatting from a selection.
Watch live word and character counts under the editor.
Download your document as an HTML file, or copy the HTML source.
keyFacts: The editor is a word-processor-style page that runs entirely in your browser.
Formatting is applied with the browser's built-in content-editing commands.
The downloaded file is a self-contained HTML document — no external files needed.
Word counts are based on the visible text, ignoring the formatting markup.
It handles English, Hindi, Arabic and any other script your keyboard can type.
